issues.display_title: Issue #67: Fix Issue "Preview" Button Loads Incorrect Folder Context from Inside Editing Tools
issues.main_description_html:
A critical context loss bug has been reported. When a user is working inside an editing tool (such as "Auto Level") within a specific folder, and they click the "Preview" button in the top navigation bar, the application routes them to the Preview screen but fails to maintain the current folder's context.

Instead of previewing the images from the folder they were just working in, the system loads a Preview state from an entirely different, previously accessed folder.

Source: user feedback (albug, Slack) — "There is a bug, let's say I am in a tool like Auto Level, and I click Preview, it takes me back to Preview from another folder, not the current folder."

Acceptance Criteria

  1. When a user is inside an editing tool (e.g., Auto Level) for Folder A, clicking "Preview" successfully opens the Preview screen populated with the images from Folder A.
  2. The application never loads images from Folder B (a previous session) when transitioning to Preview from Folder A.

🧪 Testing Scenario (for QA)

Feature: "Preview" button navigation from inside an editing tool
Goal: Verify Preview always shows the CURRENT folder's images, never a previously opened folder.

Pre-conditions

  • App running (v1.1.4+); at least two different folders with images available (call them Folder A and Folder B).

Test 1 — Core repro (current folder context preserved)

  1. Open Folder B, go to Preview at least once (to seed a previous Preview state), then leave.
  2. Open Folder A.
  3. Enter an editing tool for Folder A, e.g. Edit → Auto Level.
  4. While inside Auto Level, click Preview in the top nav.
  • ✅ Expected: Preview opens populated with Folder A images (the folder currently being worked on).
  • ❌ Fail: Preview shows Folder B images (stale/previous-session context).

Test 2 — Multiple tools

  • Repeat Test 1 using other tools (e.g. Image Minifier, AI Nadir Patching) to confirm the fix is not tool-specific.

Test 3 — Multiple folder switches

  1. Open Folder A → Preview → back.
  2. Open Folder B → enter a tool → click Preview.
  • ✅ Expected: Preview shows Folder B (the latest/current folder), not Folder A.

Test 4 — Fresh session / single folder

  1. Open only Folder A (no prior Preview history), enter a tool, click Preview.
  • ✅ Expected: Preview shows Folder A correctly (no empty/incorrect state).

Regression checks

  • Preview opened directly from File Manager still shows the correct current folder.
  • Image count and file details panel in Preview match Folder A's contents.
  • Navigating tool → Preview → back to tool keeps Folder A context intact.

Real Account Tested testergothru@gmail.com

Final Verdict Passed (Verified Smooth Wheel Zoom & Zero Parent Panel Scroll Leakage)

Technical Evaluation & Root Cause Analysis

  1. Root Cause & Previous Defect:

    • In earlier builds, the 360 panorama viewer listened to mouse wheel zoom through React's synthetic onWheel handler on the Three.js <Canvas> wrapper.
    • Because React's synthetic wheel events are treated as passive listeners by modern browser engines, calling event.preventDefault() is disallowed or ignored.
    • Consequently, when hovering over the viewer inside a scrollable layout (such as the Image to Video generator's main panel), a single mouse wheel turn simultaneously triggered camera FOV zoom and scrolled the parent container. This caused the viewer to slide away from beneath the cursor, inducing severe visual jitter and interrupted zooming.

  2. Resolution Architecture (Commit 7bcfb678):

    • As implemented in commit 7bcfb678 (fix(preview): stop wheel zoom from scrolling the parent panel), the synthetic handler was replaced with an active native DOM event listener registered via el.addEventListener('wheel', onWheel, { passive: false }).
    • The native listener executes e.preventDefault() unconditionally before delegating to handleWheel(e). This guarantees that parent scroll propagation is halted, allowing OrbitControls to adjust camera FOV smoothly while keeping the canvas firmly anchored.

3 Black Box Real Desktop App UI & Zoom Fluidity Hover cursor over 360 panorama in Image to Video, scroll wheel in and out Camera zooms in tight and out wide smoothly; viewer stays firmly anchored under cursor TP Pass

📌 Overview

Implement Keycloak-based Single Sign-On (SSO) authentication using OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow + PKCE (S256) via a native Deep Link callback (\gothru-photo-studio://auth-sso) on the Tauri v2 desktop application.

The app also features a Dynamic Auth Switcher driven by the endpoint \GET /v1/feature-flags?env=dev|live:

  • \keycloak_auth: true\ ➔ Render single Keycloak SSO Login button.
  • \keycloak_auth: false\ ➔ Fallback to the legacy manual login form (Email & Password) + Google OAuth button.

🎯 Objectives & Scope

  1. Tauri v2 Native Infrastructure:

    • Register custom deep link scheme \gothru-photo-studio\ in \ auri.conf.json.
    • Install \ auri-plugin-single-instance\ (with feature \deep-link) to ensure browser redirect callbacks refocus the existing window instead of spawning a new instance on Windows/Linux.
    • Configure capabilities \http:default\ with an explicit allowlist scope for Keycloak and GoThru API domains.
    • Register scheme at startup via \deep_link().register_all()\ for Windows/Linux dev mode.

  2. Frontend Authentication Module (\keycloak.ts):

      once.
    • Open system default browser via @tauri-apps/plugin-opener.
    • Intercept callback URL via @tauri-apps/plugin-deep-link\ listener.
    • Exchange authorization code for Keycloak tokens via @tauri-apps/plugin-http\ (CORS-free).
    • Exchange Keycloak token for GoThru session token and Session ID (\sid) via \POST /v1/auth/keycloak-login.
    • Handle backend logout via \POST /v1/auth/logout\ with payload { sid }.

  3. UI / UX Layer (\Login.tsx):

Source

User feedback

Problem

In MultiView / compare mode, 360 (equirectangular/panorama) images are arranged side by side (horizontally). Because 360 images are wide (2:1), a side-by-side layout makes each one small and hard to inspect.

Request

For 360 images, stack the views vertically — one on top of the other — instead of side by side. This gives each wide panorama more horizontal room and matches how 360 content is best compared.

Scope

  • In MultiView, change the layout so 360 images stack vertically (rows) rather than horizontally (columns).
  • Applies specifically to 360/panorama images (confirm behavior for non-360/flat images — likely keep as-is).
  • Preserve existing MultiView features (up to 8 views, sync, per-tile controls).

Acceptance Criteria
